Synopsis:
Dark Urge wakes up to the corpse of Alfira in camp.If companions are around, you will have some explaining to do.NOTE: Always put Astarion in group slot 2  if there are multiple companions

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_DarkUrge_MurderOfAlfira_GD_MorningAfter.json: The Dark Urge PC wakes in camp to find Alfira dead; if companions are present they’ll press the player for answers. Astarion is in the party (always placed in slot 2 when multiple companions) and in these lines reacts with wariness more than grief—worried that someone could get close while everyone slept. He often frames the incident as a manipulative enemy or devil “playing with us,” comparing that behavior to his old master Cazador and hinting at traumatic history. Some lines are short, location‑triggered remarks (early in play they may avoid naming his vampirism); the player’s tone (bravado, dismissal, resolve) will push Astarion toward exasperation, darker memory, or cautious agreement.
- CAMP_DarkUrge_MurderOfAlfira_CFM_AlfiraArrives.json: In this scene, Alfira arrives unannounced at the player's camp. Depending on the grove, she either 1) asks the player if she can join their camp 2) be mad at the player for upsetting her in the grove and ask to spend the night (she got lost and needs shelter) or 3) if the player has missed the grove will ask the player to come help her friends the tieflings.In all instances, when the player and Alfira go to sleep, the player will awaken to find blood on their hands and Alfira's dead body next to her. They will have killed Alfira in their sleep. This is a scene specific to the Dark Urge custom origin.
- DEN_Bard_InParty.json: Dialogue for Alfira in the brief interval when she can be a party member before the Dark Urge murders her.
- LOW_BhaalTemple_PostBattleDarkUrge_Resistance.json: Orin, Chosen of Bhaal lays dead by the Dark Urge. Bhaal has given his terms to the Dark Urge. Players has rejected Bhaal and died in the process.Players will reappear in camp.
- CAMP_AstarionHunger_PAD_AftermathAvatarCompanionLeft.json: PAD when the player wakes up to find one of the party has disappeared during the night. Astarion knows what happened - they discovered that he's a vampire and left - but doesn't want to share that information.

context: The Dark Urge origin: the PC awoke in camp to find Alfira dead beside them and blood on their hands — they killed her in their sleep after she arrived at camp and was allowed to stay. If companions are present they will demand answers; in these lines Astarion is in the party (slot 2 when multiple companions) and responds with wary, suspicious remarks rather than overt grief. He’s worried someone could get that close while everyone slept and commonly frames the scene as a manipulative enemy or devil “playing with us,” likening it to his old master Cazador and hinting at a traumatic, vampiric past (early lines may avoid naming that). The player’s tone (bravado, dismissal, or grim resolve) will push Astarion toward exasperation, darker memories, or cautious agreement.
